name: series-drawer-picks-episode
description: The series button opens the episode drawer, and picking a row applies that episode through the host by reopening it at its start rather than silently reseating the same stream.

steps.name: durationKnown
steps.note: The scrub value below is a fraction of the timeline, so the seek cannot land without a known duration.
Paused first: a running clock would make the position assertion measure elapsed time instead of the episode change.

steps.name: value
steps.note: Parks the current episode at about 7.2 s of the 12 s fixture, through the control's real 0..1 fraction. Where playback resumes after the pick separates a reopened episode from a reseated stream.
Bounded settle for the seek to reach the core.
Opens the drawer. Only visible because episodes seeded a playlist; a single-stream player keeps it hidden.

The first non-current row - index 0 is current, so playerSeriesItem is rows 1 and 2 and the click lands on episode 2. The rows carry the label as their accessible name, so this is the row a viewer reads as 'Episode 2'.

steps.name: widget_hidden
steps.note: Picking a row means "this one, now", so the drawer closes itself (PlayerDialog::goToEpisode with closeList). A click the drawer dropped leaves it open and fails here with that reason rather than passing on a stale frame.
Bounded settle for the reopened source to report its position; the assertions below carry the scenario.

assertions.note: The footer names the episode the host applied. The seeded playlist labels are Episode 1/2/3 and row index 1 is the one clicked, so a host that reseated episode 1 or ignored the pick leaves the wrong label here.
A picked episode starts at its beginning (openStream with resume=false), so the 7.2 s park must not survive. A host that reseated the same stream keeps playing from 7.2 s and fails here.

PlayerDialog::applyEpisode reopens the stream with resume=false and VideoSurface::startPendingUrl announces the new source epoch. Without this emission the host kept the old stream open and only repainted the chrome.
Picking an episode must not touch window mode; a shell whose pick path re-entered its window state machine fails here.
